topic.title: Representation Geometry and Semantic Alignment
topic.overview: Learned representations can carry useful information in different layers, modalities, or even model-weight spaces. This topic studies how to select, reshape, and align those representations so meaningful distinctions remain accessible. Representative methods use perceptual similarity, contrastive objectives, spectral structure, and geometric constraints to separate task-relevant information from nuisance variation.
topic.whyItMatters: A strong pretrained model does not guarantee that its final embedding is the best representation for a new task. Understanding geometry can improve transfer, cross-model comparison, and the construction of reusable model or dataset descriptions.
topic.evolution: The earlier examples include supervised embeddings and structured latent spaces around 2010. More recent work explores semantic translation and representation alignment across models. The 2026 papers extend this perspective to layerwise subspace selection and contrastive alignment between datasets and neural-network weights, illustrating several distinct uses of geometry rather than a single lineage.
openQuestions: Which geometric properties predict transfer before downstream labels are available?
How can alignment preserve meaningful differences rather than erase them?
